title: Common BIDMAS Mistakes
welcome_lead: Avoid the traps. Many BIDMAS errors come from rushing. Learn to spot them and stay accurate.
meta_desc: Avoid common BIDMAS mistakes in this KS3 maths adventure.
final_note: Superb! You are now BIDMAS-mistake proof.

concepts.def: Test your answer to confirm correctness.
Working through carefully one move at a time.

walkthroughs.body_html:
For 8 − 3 + 2, you must go left to right.

8 − 3 = 5, then 5 + 2 = 7. Not 8 − 5 = 3 (wrong).

For 2 + 3 × 4, multiplication is done first.

3 × 4 = 12, then 2 + 12 = 14. Not (2 + 3) × 4 = 20 (wrong).

options: 7, because you do 12 / 2 = 6 and then add 3 with the multiplication symbol meaning 'and'.
9, because you add all the numbers and then subtract the operator count.
14, because you read and calculate left to right (3 + 4 = 7, then 7 x 2).
11 — multiplication is done before addition (3 + 8 = 11).
2, because in BIDMAS multiplication comes before division (12 / 6).
18 — division and multiplication share the same precedence; work left to right (6 x 3).
-15, because two negatives multiply to give a larger negative result.

-15, because two negatives multiply to give a larger negative result.
2 — subtracting a negative is the same as adding, so -3 + 5 = 2.

-8, because two negatives combine to make a bigger negative.
